implementationBoundary.changed: Private SQL-payload decode/materialization path only, plus clearing its per-store memo after dispose drains.
unchanged: SQLite schema, WAL, synchronous=FULL, BEGIN IMMEDIATE, writer admission and retry timeout
SQL SELECT statements and three-surface observation order
Callback execution/return semantics and domain algorithms
CurrentSnapshots and staged nested-read encode/decode roundtrips
Commit validation, blob operations and generation checks
Authentication payload reads, expiry and atomic take/removal
implementationBoundary.memo: Per-open-store map with at most one entry per surface, at most three entries. A frozen record holds only original payload, compact JSON, JSON-encoded undefined paths and a numeric string-length charge. No decoded graph, callback result, grant, Request, session binding or credential bytes is retained in the memo.
implementationBoundary.hitCondition: The just-observed SQL payload string must equal the complete validated original payload string. No version, object identity, function identity, digest approximation or payload-length equality substitutes for it.
implementationBoundary.hitBehavior: JSON.parse creates a new graph; -0 is emitted as a native JSON numeric literal; null placeholders are restored to own enumerable/writable/configurable undefined properties with Object.defineProperty. Object key order and dense arrays match the unchanged decoder.
implementationBoundary.missBehavior: Delete the previous entry for that surface, run the complete unchanged v1 decoder/validator before creating an optional plan. Missing SQL rows delete the old entry and synthesize the unchanged empty snapshot. Invalid rows throw before user callback.
implementationBoundary.writeBehavior: Only previously observed SQL input bytes may be retained. Mutated callback snapshots and write outcomes are not inserted. All commit=true writes still encode and independently decode/validate before SQL writes and COMMIT.

invariants.invariant: Prove less actual snapshot work on representative SQLite state before the original journey.
invariants.mechanism: Warm exact-payload materialization replaces the recursive tagged decoder and its tuple/object assembly with fresh compact JSON parsing plus bounded undefined restoration.
invariants.expected: Cold parse count equals present SQL rows and their total characters. Warm transaction tagged parse count and encode descriptor reads are zero, object assemblies at most three; direct decode remains an independent full tagged-work control with more than 1000 entry tuples. Both outputs re-encode to identical persisted bytes.
limits: S1 counters and test outcomes are observed. Selection failure remains explicit; these passing short proofs do not close FIN-IND-005.
Six interleaved timing samples are observations, never pass/fail ratio or whole-journey acceleration proof.
Scoped currentSnapshots/nestedRead timings exclude outer admission and must not be added to transaction timings.

invariants.invariant: Preserve fresh SQL observations even at identical versions and payload length.
invariants.mechanism: Each read still SELECTs under the existing transaction/lock; exact string comparison happens after the SELECT. Changed bytes, deleted rows or malformed payloads invalidate the prior surface entry.
invariants.expected: Same-length same-version replacement is observed, deletion yields empty state, restoration is re-read, malformed rows reject before callback. Case read/draft/prepare-intent races still suppress stale disclosure.
limits: The SQL content tests cover selected races and malformed examples, not all possible filesystem faults.
No claim of eliminating SQL reads or lock admission cost.

invariants.invariant: No mutable state or callback outputs are shared between requests.
invariants.mechanism: Every hit parses a new full object graph. Plans contain strings rather than callback objects, and are built before callbacks mutate the snapshot. Existing provider clone boundaries remain intact.
invariants.expected: Mutating retained read, declined-write, committed-write, opaque-callback or egress-observed objects cannot change the next request or durable SQL state.
limits: Persisted financial results remain data in the byte-equivalent snapshot representation; no previously authorized response, result object or predicate outcome is reused.
These tests do not prove behavior for arbitrary monkey-patched platform intrinsics.

invariants.invariant: Preserve principal, Request, header, binding, lease and source-authority fences.
invariants.mechanism: The memo never receives authority inputs or callback results. State-provider and case-port are untouched; original authorize/revalidate/request/source checks execute on each observation.
invariants.expected: Principal mismatch, Request replacement, header mutation, revocation, mutable/accessor binding changes, ended leases and final case mutations suppress values as before.
limits: S01 uses the in-memory testPersistence adapter and is supplementary only.
The synthetic authority/empty-case tests are not installed native-session acceptance.
Full financial source/replay assertions still require the unchanged original journey.

invariants.invariant: Preserve transactions, WAL, admission ordering, CAS and one callback execution.
invariants.mechanism: BEGIN IMMEDIATE, writer queue, waitForAdmission, retryLock, transaction ownership and callback execution code are unchanged; the memo is read only after the fresh locked SELECT.
invariants.expected: Independent warm stores serialize same-version writers; one wins and the other sees fresh version and declines. Different-record changes survive, callbacks are not replayed, cancelled/timed-out admissions do not overtake their predecessor.
limits: No new cross-process crash or power-loss injection is introduced.
Durability remains SQLite's existing FULL/WAL contract, with reopen/concurrency regression coverage.
The selected namespace-isolation test fails on extra sfBlobGenerations metadata. B1 reproduced the exact failure on the unchanged preimage; the test and overall S1 selection still remain FAIL.

invariants.invariant: Abort, callback throw, rejected writes and invalid commits cannot publish state or blobs.
invariants.mechanism: Signal checks, commit=false behavior, final ROLLBACK and error propagation are unchanged. A memo entry describes only input read from SQL; it never contains staged mutation outputs.
invariants.expected: After abort/throw/invalid snapshots, original snapshot and document bytes remain, orphan blobs do not exist, and reopen observes the unchanged state.
limits: No injected low-level disk-full or COMMIT I/O failure in the new tests; existing validation and transaction mechanics are retained by source inspection.

invariants.invariant: Nested reads see staged state without sharing it, and caught nested writes poison the enclosing transaction.
invariants.mechanism: Staged parent snapshots retain the original encode/decode clone path, not the SQL-payload memo. Parent/root readers, poisoned flags, scope checks and nested blob-write rejection are unchanged.
invariants.expected: Child/currentSnapshots mutations do not change the parent's staged object; uncommitted staged values are visible to nested reads; caught forbidden writes still prevent parent commit.
limits: The optimization does not reduce staged snapshot cloning work.
The currentSnapshots path remains intentionally unoptimized.

invariants.invariant: Closed callback scopes and disposed stores reject later use while admitted operations drain.
invariants.mechanism: requireScope, context ownership and capability checks are unchanged. dispose adds memo.clear only after Promise.allSettled of already active operations.
invariants.expected: Late currentSnapshots/blob capabilities fail, live children cannot outlive successful parent completion, admitted work drains, new operations are denied.
limits: Tests do not inspect private map entries or measure immediate garbage collection; bounded retention and dispose clearing are source-verified.

invariants.invariant: Preserve blobs, private generations and atomicity with state.
invariants.mechanism: No blob bytes enter the materialization plan. Blob SQL reads/writes/removal, generation increment/overflow checks and generation-integrity checks stay inside the same existing transaction.
invariants.expected: Rollback restores prior blob state; namespace separation and concurrent mixed state/blob workloads survive; backup restore retains matching snapshot/blob content.
limits: The memo may serialize generation metadata as ordinary snapshot data, with fresh detached reconstruction.
No change to blob storage format or backup lifecycle.
Namespace-isolation comparison fails on sfBlobGenerations metadata, while the other listed blob/rollback tests pass. B1 reproduced the same failure on the preimage; overall S1 selection remains FAIL.

invariants.invariant: Credential/session reads remain fresh and independent of business locks and snapshot optimization.
invariants.mechanism: Authentication methods are unchanged and do not call loadSnapshot. secrets.get still queries expiry-filtered SQL without a write lock and returns fresh Uint8Array bytes.
invariants.expected: Mutating returned secret bytes does not affect later reads; expiration, independent-store update and removal are observed inside and outside a business transaction.
limits: No claim of new identity-provider or external credential-system validation.

invariants.invariant: Preserve v1 values, exact re-encoding, property order, special names and compatibility.
invariants.mechanism: Persisted encoder/decoder are unchanged. Only validated normalized decoder output is converted. Direct JSON emission avoids toJSON invocation; native -0 literals preserve negative zero; known own-path fixups preserve undefined and property insertion order, including __proto__.
invariants.expected: Warm/reopened objects re-encode byte-identically; integer/empty/special/escaped keys, null-prototype input normalization, nonenumerable input normalization, sparse-array normalization, tagged-looking arrays, lone surrogates and owned undefined retain original decoder semantics.
limits: This is equivalence over the v1 codec's accepted normalized value domain, not arbitrary JavaScript objects.
Nonenumerable/sparse/null-prototype inputs are normalized exactly as the existing codec; original input descriptors/prototypes are not newly promised.

invariants.invariant: Malformed state and invalid future writes must still fail closed.
invariants.mechanism: Every new SQL payload runs the complete old decodeSnapshot; exact-equal validated strings alone permit memoization. All commits still use encodeSnapshot plus decodeSnapshot. Existing accessor/prototype/symbol/cycle/type rejection remains in encode.
invariants.expected: Malformed JSON/envelope/duplicate keys/negative version reject before callback; accessors are not executed during encoding; inherited-prototype writes fail; invalid product-state outcomes are preserved.
limits: The test corpus is representative and does not enumerate every malformed v1 node combination.
A validated identical payload need not repeat the pure validator; this is byte-equivalent memoization, not validation skipped on version/function identity.

invariants.invariant: Bound retained decoder-plan resources without introducing new acceptance limits.
invariants.mechanism: At most three per-store entries; sum of original payload, compact JSON and encoded undefined-path string lengths is at most 8*1024*1024 UTF-16 code units. Admission evicts oldest entries until within the aggregate bound. Plan traversal stops above depth 128, 200000 nodes or 4096 undefined fixups; a failed plan leaves the original decoded result valid and uncached.
invariants.expected: Oversized and traversal-limited valid snapshots retain bytes and special values and repeat full tagged decoding; cycling the three individually cacheable large surfaces produces misses rather than exceeding aggregate retention.
limits: 16 MiB means retained UTF-16 string content at two bytes per charged code unit, not total heap/RSS.
The bound excludes JS object/Map overhead, temporary parse/planning arrays, active callback/output graphs, SQLite memory and other independent open stores.
No native heap profiler or GC timing proof is claimed.
Fallback is an optimization limit only; legacy acceptance limits and errors remain unchanged.

invariants.invariant: Reopen and backup restore preserve exact state without migration.
invariants.mechanism: No on-disk schema, snapshot envelope or writer codec change. The per-store memo is empty on open and is discarded after dispose drains. Existing backup code continues full encode/decode structural checks and snapshotSha256 validation.
invariants.expected: Warm-store disposal/reopen and real capture/restore preserve state, undefined/-0 and blobs; corrupt archives fail before target changes.
limits: Reopen is not a simulated OS crash or power-loss experiment.
No original financial historical-choice/replay/reopen assertion is satisfied merely by these storage tests.

migrationRollback.diskFormat: Unchanged sucafina-snapshot envelope version 1; unchanged SQLite tables and writes.
migrationRollback.forwardCompatibility: Existing valid v1 rows are decoded by the unchanged validator on the first observation. Cold stores do not depend on a previous process's memo.
migrationRollback.rollbackOfMission34: Reverting only mission34's local-store.ts optimization to received baseline returns to full decoding and reads the same persisted v1 bytes; no data rewrite or migration is required. This conclusion is scoped to the unchanged snapshot codec and should not be generalized to earlier Finance business-receipt revisions.
migrationRollback.mixedVersionBoundary: New and received-baseline store implementations still use identical SQLite transaction and snapshot formats; the short tests cover independent current-version instances, not a mixed-binary deployment.
migrationRollback.predecessorBoundary: Mission18's compact Finance receipts and all other prior business changes are preserved. Their separate older-reader rollback caveats are not waived by snapshot compatibility.
migrationRollback.performanceOnRollback: Expected loss of the optimization only; no performance-budget guarantee for the old decoder.
